albums.blurb: Yusef Lateef was a Detroit multi-instrumentalist who moved between tenor saxophone, flute, and oboe, and one of the first American jazz musicians to fold Middle and Far Eastern instruments and scales into small-group jazz. Eastern Sounds was cut in September 1961 for Prestige's Moodsville imprint with pianist Barry Harris, bassist Ernie Farrow, and drummer Lex Humphries, among the last recordings of the Detroit band Lateef brought to New York. Alongside its blues and ballads it works the xun (a Chinese globular flute) and the rabab into the quartet, and includes Lateef's oboe readings of the film themes from Spartacus and The Robe.
albums.reception: AllMusic rates the album five stars and calls it one of Lateef's most enduring recordings.

albums.blurb: Phony Ppl are a Brooklyn band of five childhood friends, fronted by singer Elbee Thrie, who came up through the borough's jam-session scene and produce their records themselves, playing everything live. mō'zā-ik. is their third album and the follow-up to 2015's Yesterday's Tomorrow: eleven tracks that fold jazz harmony, funk bass, and bossa nova touches into contemporary R&B songwriting.
albums.reception: NPR premiered the album as a First Listen, and it carries a 90 critic score on the review aggregator Album of the Year.

albums.blurb: Masayoshi Takanaka is a Tokyo guitarist who came up through the Sadistic Mika Band — the first Japanese rock band to tour the UK, opening for Roxy Music in 1975 — and its successor the Sadistics before going solo with 1976's Seychelles. An Insatiable High, his third solo album, was recorded in 1977 at Larrabee Sound in Los Angeles with the Tower of Power horn section, guitarist Lee Ritenour, keyboardist Patrice Rushen, and bassist Chuck Rainey, with session singer Jim Gilstrap handling the vocals on the title track. Its sunny, tropical guitar fusion set the template for the run of albums that made Takanaka one of Japan's most popular instrumentalists.
albums.reception: On the review aggregator Album of the Year it holds an 86/100 user score from more than 1,600 ratings, ranking tenth among the site's albums of 1977.
